summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Junkei Washio studied at Toyo University from circa 1887 to 1891. He later held posts at Toyo University, Sendan-Rin School, and Komazawa University.

Specializing in Indology and Buddhist studies, Junkichi Imanishi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1960–1966). He taught at Hokkaido University (~1970–1996), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (~1996–2011), and directed the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (~2004–2017).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and Indology, Junko Matsumura studied at the Australian National University (MA, 1980) and the University of Göttingen (PhD, 1990). Matsumura is attested as a professor at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies in 2011.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Junko Minamoto studied at Otani University and held a post at Kansai University.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, Junsho Kato studied at KU Leuven, under Étienne Lamotte, Akira Hirakawa, and Hajime Nakamura, and earned a PhD from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Nishogakusha University and Nagoya University.

Specializing in philosophy and sinology, Junyi Tang studied at Peking University and under Thomé H. Fang and Shili Xiong. He held posts at National Central University (circa 1937–1949) and New Asia Institute of Advanced Chinese Studies (circa 1949–1978).
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Junzo Inagaki studied under Shoshin Fukihara and held a post as section chief at Otani University.
Specializing in Indology and philosophy, Juro Watanabe studied under Gerhard Oberhammer and held a post at the University of Tsukuba, attested from 1989 to 1990.
A scholar of Buddhist studies, Jushu Nakasone held posts at Bukkyo University as a part-time lecturer (attested 2005) and at Kyoto Bunkyo Junior College (attested 2020).

Specializing in Buddhist studies and religious studies, Justin McDaniel served as Associate Professor of Religious Studies at the University of California, Riverside, and Professor of Religious Studies at the University of Pennsylvania (attested 2011–2018).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies, Justin R. Ritzinger completed a PhD at Harvard University under Robert M. Gimello and Michael Puett. He held posts at Dharma Drum Mountain, Dharma Drum Buddhist College, Academia Sinica, and Oberlin College.
Specializing in philosophy, Justin Shimeld earned a PhD from the University of Tasmania (attested 2012), where he studied under doctoral supervisors Jeff Malpas and Sonam Thakchoe.

Specializing in linguistics and Iranian and Central Asian studies, Justus Olshausen studied at Kiel, Berlin, and under Silvestre de Sacy, Langlès, and Kieffer. He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1827–1853) and the University of Königsberg (~1853–1858).

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, János Szerb studied at Eötvös Loránd University (~1975–1980). He was a research associate and lecturer at the University of Vienna (1982) and a researcher at the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (~1985–1988).
Specializing in Buddhist studies and Japanology, Jérôme Ducor studied under Jacques May (~1975–1985). He held a post at the University of Lausanne around 2005.

Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, Józef Kowalewski studied at Vilnius University and Kazan Imperial University. He held posts at Kazan Imperial University (~1828–1860), serving as rector in 1855, and at the University of Warsaw (~1862–1878).
Specializing in linguistics, József Budenz studied under Theodor Benfey at the University of Göttingen (~1855–1858). He later held a post at Eötvös Loránd University from circa 1872 to 1892.

Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Jörg Heimbel studied at Tibet University and completed a PhD at the University of Hamburg (2014) under David P. Jackson, Dorji Wangchuk, and Franz-Karl Ehrhard. He was attested as a Hamburg lecturer in 2019.
Specializing in Buddhist studies and sinology, Jörg Plassen has served as a professor at Geumgang University and at Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2013).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies, Jørn Borup earned his PhD at Aarhus University (~1998–2002) under Armin W. Geertz and Ian Reader. He later served as an associate professor at Aarhus University (~2007–2023).
